Reporting Statements
You can use reporting verbs followed by a that-clause when you report what other people say.
Vanessa said we needed to buy all these spices.
When you report what people say in your own words, you use reporting verbs like say, think, mention and so on. Most times you use a that-clause after these verbs
The singer said that she had been singing since she was a child.
In speaking or informal usage, it is also okay to leave out that. You can also leave out that with other more frequently used reporting verbs such as agree, mention, promise, notice and warn.

The actress said (that) she was looking forward to working with Steven Spielberg.
The director mentioned (that) the movie was being filmed in Ireland.

Unlikely Conditionals: Should in the If-Clause
You can use a conditional sentence to talk about unlikely events in the present and future.
If you should have any questions, text me.
You can form an unlikely conditional with would in the main clause and if + simple past in the if-clause.
You can also use should in the if-clause with a similar effect. It shows the possibility of the condition as well as the unlikelihood of it happening.
When you use should in the if-clause, the meaning is similar to the less formal expression by any chance.

• If the man should admit to the crime, the police would press charges. (The man is unlikely to admit to the crime, but if he does, the police would press charges.)
  • If by any chance you see Maria, tell her that class has been cancelled. (It is unlikely that you will see Maria, but if you do, tell her that class has been cancelled.)
You can also change the if-clause structure and begin with<span class="strong"> should. This is a more formal structure.

• Should the man admit to the crime, the police would press charges
    • .
  • Should you see Maria, tell her that class has been cancelled.
If you should see any maple syrup we can get that too.
Should you try it, you'll find it has a bitter aftertaste.
Should you see lentils, don't forget to pick some up.

images.text:
Vanessa: Okay, here we are at the supermarket. I'm got to check out the prices of a few things for the restaurant so you two start and I'll meet you in the produce section in 10 minutes. If you should have any questions, text me.
Amy: Okay. So let's start with our basics list. Vanessa said we needed to buy all these spices. Cinnamon, turmeric, ginger, and sea salt. She promised that adding spices would make any vegetarian recipe more flavorful. She's really resolved and bent on us doing this cleanse.
Peter: I asked her about using honey as a sweetener and she replied that it was okay. So we should get a big jar of honey. If you should see any maple syrup we can get that too. Vanessa explained that you can replace sugar in dessert recipes with honey, maple syrup or stevia.

Amy: I really don't like stevia. Should you try it, you'll find it has a bitter aftertaste.
Peter: Okay, we won't get that.
Amy: We also need some vegetable stock and some root vegetables.
Peter: Okay. I'll grab those.
Amy: Next we need to pick up green vegetables like celery, cucumber, broccoli and avocado. Vanessa reported that they are great detoxifiers.
Peter: Wow, you're a real eager beaver! I'm really glad you're doing this with me. I think I'd be really apathetic if I had to do this on my own.

Amy: I'm glad I'm doing it too. I think we're going to feel rejuvenated when we're done.
Now, next on the list is legumes. Let's get chick peas and beans. Should you see lentils, don't forget to pick some up. I want to make that lentil stew.
Peter: Fine. I'll get lentils but I'm not eating them.
Amy: Peter, sometimes you are so childish.
